findings.description: Issuer-pubkey trust gap at ucan_blobs_protocol::validate_request ARM 5. The wave-3e handler validates AuthorizationGrant.binding_sig using the issuer_verifying_key bytes EMBEDDED IN THE GRANT ITSELF (authorization_grant.rs:670 `VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&vk_bytes)` where `vk_bytes` is `self.issuer_verifying_key`). The handler does NOT chain that issuer-pubkey to a trusted root or known issuer-DID anywhere in the 6-arm pipeline. An attacker who controls any keypair can self-mint a grant with arbitrary (ucan, key_material, audience, scope) bytes, sign with their own key, embed their pubkey in `issuer_verifying_key`, and verify_binding will return Ok(()). The doc-comment at ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:273-275 ('the production wire-up accepts grants issued by other principals through the chain validator at the cap-policy hook') acknowledges the gap but no specific destination row is named in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md for this READ-side issuer-trust seam. (Distinct from §4.23's WRITE-side user-DID root-chain validator + distinct from Row D-26's PQ-hybrid wire-in.) At wave-3e fixtures the handler-keypair IS the grant issuer so tests stay self-consistent and never exercise the cross-issuer adversarial case. CLOSING THE GAP IS WAVE-3E PRODUCTION SCOPE not v1-beta-tag scope, BUT the named-destination must exist per HARD RULE 12.
findings.evidence: crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:496-499 (ARM 5 verify_binding call with no upstream issuer-trust check); crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:653-695 (verify_binding parses issuer_verifying_key from self with NO trust-anchor); crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:269-275 (doc-comment naming 'production wire-up' chain validator at 'cap-policy hook' but no specific row in DEFERRED.md).
findings.recommendation: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW destination = either (a) add a new Row D-NN in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md naming the read-side issuer-trust seam at validate_request_for_connection ARM 5 with explicit destination = the G-CORE-3e production-wire-up wave or G-COMP-1 sync hardening sub-wave; OR (b) extend Row D-15-cluster (S&C runtime carries) to enumerate this gap if it semantically fits there. Per HARD RULE 12 the deferral disposition is acceptable AS LONG AS the destination row is minted NOW. Author-time the row, then re-dispose-as-deferred.

findings.description: Hybrid signature commitment comparison at sig.rs:473 uses Vec<u8> PartialEq which is non-constant-time. For a SHA3-256 commitment over PUBLIC inputs (pubkeys + sigs + msg are all public-known at verify time), timing leakage doesn't compromise secret material — the security property is preimage resistance of SHA3-256, not commitment-equality secrecy. The subtle::ConstantTimeEq pattern is the textbook recommendation for any crypto-equality comparison; subtle is already a workspace dep (crypto-suite Cargo.toml). Discipline-note rather than fix-now.
findings.evidence: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/sig.rs:471-477 (commitment_expected != sig.commitment); subtle crate at crypto-suite Cargo.toml (already workspace dep).
findings.recommendation: OBSERVATION ONLY — no fix-now required since the comparison inputs are public. If future R6 rounds surface ANY cryptographic-equality comparison whose inputs include secret material, codify a pim-N for 'subtle::ConstantTimeEq for crypto-equality compare' across the workspace + sweep this site to that standard then for consistency. Discipline-note can be carried at the bottom of authorization_grant.rs / sig.rs doc-blocks naming the public-input rationale.
